subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm planning the knight's skeleton structure, thinking through a humanoid rig with hips, spine, neck, head, and a jointed helm with a separate jaw/chin-guard piece, arranged in an A-pose facing forward.

Working out exact joint coordinates for hip, spine, neck, and head heights, then starting to chain shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints for the arms using directional vectors for the A-pose stance.

I'm continuing the leg chain with hip, knee, ankle, and toe positions spaced slightly apart, then thinking through weapon placement -- deciding whether the sword hangs point-down in the right hand with the shield mounted on the left arm, or whether the sword should be planted vertically in front like a resting knight.

Working out the right arm's shoulder-to-wrist vector so the hand lands at hip height with the sword blade angled down toward the floor.

Blade extends up to y1.95, that at-the-ready pose clears everything fine. Now for the left arm, I'm bending the forearm forward too and positioning a kite shield on the outer side, facing forward at roughly x=0.4, z=0.3, sized about 0.45 wide by 1.0 tall, with the arm tucked behind it so it doesn't collide.

I'm defining the kite shield shape as an extruded outline in the XY plane with the thickness pushed along +Z, tracing a rounded top that tapers to a point at the bottom with a slight bevel and sharp tip. For the emblem, I'm planning a simplified silver griffin silhouette rendered as an SVG texture/decal on the shield face.

I'll apply decals using the shield part and torso surface as targets, sizing and orienting them to sit flush on the front — the shield decal roughly 0.34 by 0.5 meters, and the torso decal on the surcoat chest, since parts and lofted sweeps both work as valid surface targets. Now I'm sketching the griffin SVG itself, composing a body, head, and wings in a silver fill with dark stroke within a simple viewBox.

For the shoulder armor, I'm planning layered lame plates with gold trim and a mirrored filigree decal on the top piece, using dome-shaped sphere geometry for the pauldrons. For the steel surfaces I'm considering mottled paint textures to suggest dents and wear.

Bumping paint size to 2048 for better texture resolution, and considering adding shallow dark discs as dents on the breastplate, perhaps using a spots function nested within the mottle paint to simulate scattered damage.

I'm defining the armor material by layering mottle and spots paint functions with specific colors and seeds for a worn, scratched metal look, keeping within a 64-color limit since painted parts share materials. Now I'm setting up helper functions for building geometry primitives like boxes, cylinders, and spheres, plus a part-adding helper that attaches geometry to bones at specific positions.

I'm figuring out how to connect limb segments using rods and capsules bound to single joints for uniform weight painting, then starting to lay out the actual body design—hips, belt, and a tabard-style surcoat built from frustum boxes spanning the torso.

Working out the frustumBox orientation math, computing cross products to determine which local axis becomes the width direction when the shape points downward, so the surcoat panels get the right proportions.

Now I'm laying out the torso parts: a breastplate frustum tapering from chest to waist, a small ridge detail down the center, and a surcoat panel hanging from chest to knees with its own tapering dimensions.

I'll add a tabard with a flared, gold-trimmed hem, attaching it rigidly near the hips/spine. I'm also adding a brown belt with a gold buckle at the waist, and narrowing the front panel to 0.28 so the armor plating shows at the sides.

Now I'm placing a griffin decal on the panel front and checking that it projects correctly onto the sweep geometry. Then I'm layering stacked lame plates for the abdomen faulds hidden under the surcoat, adding angled tassets on the thighs, and draping a torn crimson cape behind the shoulders using a polygon slab shape.

I'm plotting the ragged cape outline point by point, letting the top edge sit close to the body and tilting the bottom edge further back along z so the cape appears to hang naturally away from the figure.

For the cape's surface detail, I'm using a stripe fill with dark crimson tones and some wobble along the x-axis to suggest loose vertical folds rather than a flat slab, which should give it a bit of fabric-like depth.

Now I'm designing the great helm as a lathe shape so I get a smoothly curved profile from radius and height points, building out a rounded crown with a slightly sloped top rather than a plain cylinder.

I'm splitting the helm into two separate pieces -- an upper skull piece and a lower bevor/jaw piece -- with a hinge point at the back of the jaw so the jaw could potentially pivot open.

Still shaping the helm geometry... adding an eye slit box and a vertical reinforcement cross-band on the front surface.

Adding gold trim torus rings at the helm base, then building the crimson plume with a crest holder and a swept, tapering path from front-top to back.

Working out the arc positions for the crest tufts...

I'll use 11 feathers with alternating crimson tones for the plume, reaching a total height around 2.12, plus a steel gorget with rings at the neck. For the shoulders, I'm layering pauldrons with three stacked dome-like lames using partial spheres.

Still writing geometry for the pauldron tilts...

Scaling composes before the baked rotation, so the torus thickness just gets squashed vertically a bit, which is fine. Now I'm placing a gold filigree decal on the outer visible part of the largest lame, positioning it outward along the lame's curve with a normal direction and a small size so it reads as ornamental trim.

For the filigree texture itself, I'm sketching a simple SVG with scroll-like gold stroke paths, no fill, over a transparent background so only the thin lines show through via alpha testing, then planning to apply it to both lame 2 and lame 3.

For the arms, I'm building shoulder-to-elbow rerebrace capsules, spherical elbow cops with gold trim, tapered forearm vambraces, and boxy gauntlets with separated fingers and thumb — trying to keep a simple joint budget per hand with a palm box plus four finger segments.

For the hands I'll make a generic function with palm at the wrist and fingers extending along the forearm direction; the right hand needs curled fingers wrapping around the sword grip while the left stays more open for the shield strap, so I'm positioning finger boxes horizontally across the grip to fake a wrap without too many extra joints.

For the left hand gripping the shield handle, I'll mirror the same fist structure with a vertical grip bar. Now I'm working out the hand positions, starting with the right arm's shoulder joint and tracing the upper arm direction to find the elbow location.

Checking the shield's position relative to the body — centering it around chest height with width spanning roughly x=.11 to .61, placing its back face near z=.31 so it sits just behind the hand without clipping into the leg or torso. It mostly obscures the left arm, which is fine for the knight pose, but I want to confirm the top edge height doesn't look off.

Now I'm designing the shield construction: a gold rim extrude slightly larger and thicker behind, a blue face extrude slightly smaller in front so the rim shows as a border, plus a griffin decal on the face and small scratch marks for wear and realism.

Placing the griffin decal on the shield's front face with proper offset and lift, then moving to leg armor pieces: thigh cuisses, knee poleyns with fins, greaves, and sabaton boots built from boxes and wedges.

Working out the foot geometry with a box base and sphere-scaled toe cap joined at the ankle, plus setting up the toe bone joint and leg segment proportions from hip to knee.

Now I'm computing leg lengths and capsule radii for thighs and shins, checking that the hip-to-knee-to-ankle chain fits without overlap, and nudging the knee and ankle slightly outward for a natural stance. I'm also considering how to structure the skeletal joint hierarchy, deciding whether to use a chain helper for the spine path from hips through spine segments up toward the neck base.

Continuing the chain with a neck segment up to the head joint, then adding a jaw joint parented to the head with a forward-facing direction for hinge rotation.

Now I'm setting up the leg chains with hip, knee, and ankle joints, using three names per side so the ankle becomes the tip joint, then adding a toe joint parented off the ankle, with left/right suffixes determined by side sign. I'm mirroring this approach for the arm chains, naming shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints per side.

Then I'm working out the hand and finger structure parented off the wrist, using capsules for the upper arm and forearm bones tied to the shoulder and elbow joints respectively, and starting to assemble the sword parts — grip, pommel, and crossguard — attached to the right wrist bone.

Now shaping the blade geometry with an extruded outline, tapering width and thickness toward the tip, adding a center fuller groove, and placing small edge notches for battle wear.

I realize the fuller box would protrude slightly beyond the blade's thin cross-section at mid-length, but I'll let it stand as a raised rib detail since it reads fine visually. For positioning, I need to compute the grip center in code, then derive pommel and guard positions relative to it, with the blade starting where the guard ends and extending upward.

Now I'm figuring out hand and finger placement for both the sword grip and shield handle: computing wrist-relative offsets for the palm box and gauntlet armor, then placing four finger blocks stacked vertically with small offsets to simulate a closed fist.

Positioning the thumb joint relative to the palm, then adding gold trim rings at the elbow and wrist using torus shapes oriented along the forearm direction.

I'm estimating total part count around 200, confirming paint works fine across sweeps and extrudes, and bumping up paintSize to 2048 for texture density before settling on flat gold and dark gold color values.

Finalizing the remaining color palette for crimson, blue, leather, and dark steel tones, then deciding to skip gold trim on the breastplate while adding small dark dent spheres on the pauldrons, helm, and greaves for extra detail.

Now I'm adding scratch marks as thin pale rotated boxes scattered across the helm and shield, and placing small gold clasp spheres with a connecting rod near the shoulders to simulate cape fasteners.

I'm checking the cape's position relative to the pauldrons and legs, making sure its width and depth fall naturally behind the armor without clipping through the shoulders or legs, and considering adding a second torn layer piece behind it for depth.

For the shoulder area, I'm adding a mantle-style crimson box across the shoulders with gold trim, attached to the spine3 bone, then moving into building the cuirass shape using a tapered frustum box from chest to waist.

I'm deciding to skip a chest bulge and instead cover the upper torso with a surcoat panel starting around y 1.38, leaving a gap at the collar so steel breastplate and gold trim show through, with the panel narrower than the torso so edges peek out on each side, plus side straps and a griffin emblem placed on the chest panel.

Now I'm working out the panel's depth and dimensions using a tapered box shape between two points, adding a gold hem trim strip at the bottom, and mirroring a similar back panel hidden mostly by the cape. Then I'm positioning a steel pelvis box at the hips and a leather belt box just above it near the waist.

Belt sits over the surcoat, wrapping as a wide shallow box; I'm also extending the cuirass taper down from the chest to the waist, narrowing its width and depth as it goes.

Adding hip tassets as small steel boxes beside the belt, then working out the gorget placement to fit under the helm's jaw piece without overlapping, flaring the cylinder radii to meet the shoulders.

Now I'm sketching the griffin SVG itself: silver fill with dark strokes, building the tail as a curved path, the raised rear wing as a layered feather silhouette, and starting the lion-like body shape.

I need to make sure the rig root is set up correctly, and that decals on the frustum box sweep across the surface targets with proper bone weights. Now I'm starting to write the actual build function, setting up the builder with a knight rig and paint texture, then applying mottle effects for the worn battle texture with configurable size, seed, and contrast.

Writing material helpers...

Building the joint hierarchy now... setting hips as the root, then chaining the spine upward through three segments, followed by a short neck chain connecting to the top spine joint.

Adding head and jaw joints next... and now looping through left and right legs, defining hip, knee, and ankle positions as a three-point chain, then attaching toe joints at the ankle.

For leg geometry, I'm adding thigh capsules from hip to knee, a steel sphere for the knee cap, and a small gold cone spike angled forward as decorative detail.

Adding more leg geometry...

Now computing the arm joint positions - shoulder, elbow, wrist - and deriving the hand/grip location by projecting forward from the forearm direction so the fist sits naturally at the end.

Adding wrist cuff rings and building layered pauldron shoulder plates...

Working out the shoulder tilt direction and lame positioning... for positive side the rotation should be negative so the dome leans correctly, and I'm placing each lame's x-offset and y-position so they overlap slightly in a stacked armor pattern.

Adjusting the lame heights to sit closer to the shoulder joint and planning a filigree decal placement on the lower lames, anchored relative to each lame's radius and mirrored for the opposite side.

Simplifying: the ray just needs to approximately hit the surface, so I don't need exact rotation correctness. With the dome tilted, I'm computing the decal direction as the rotated axis vector and placing the center point along that axis offset by the dome radius.

Visible parts of lame 3's top get covered by lame 2 sitting above it, and lame 2's top gets covered by lame 1, leaving only thin visible bands near the rims. Rather than hand-deriving the rotated coordinates with sines and cosines, I'll just use a vector rotation utility to handle the tilt transform properly.

Still computing lame positions...

Placing dents...

Adding scratches on flat-facing surfaces: shield face, helm front, and upper cuirass chest area above the surcoat line. For the helm, I'm defining a lathed profile with radius/height points to shape the dome and taper, which pushes the crown up higher than expected, so I'll set the plume base around y=1.89 to match.

Rechecking plume base after the helm height shift, and confirming the eye slit position lines up with the helm's vertical offset. I'm also deciding between smooth shading with 12 segments versus a faceted low-poly look with 10 segments, where rotating the spin angle by 18° centers a flat face toward the front instead of an edge.

Positioning the slit...

I realize the flat band would float off the curved decagon surface at its edges, so instead I should wrap the trim as a proper lathe-generated ring around the helm that follows the surface contour.

Thinking through the slit geometry more, I'm narrowing it to .075 wide so it reads as an eye slit, then adding a vertical center band (.02 wide, z .118) across the slit to split it into two halves for the classic helm look, keeping it just proud of the front face surface.

Now I'm positioning breath holes on the jaw: small dark boxes arranged in rows near y 1.56-1.60, kept within the narrow front face width, roughly six total, skipping side holes for simplicity. The upper helm top is a flat cap finished via lathe.

I'm placing the crest holder as a small steel box, then working out the plume's radial fan geometry—elongated sphere elements spreading from a center point behind the helm, extending forward and back in z and up in y, with a thin crest rail bar near the base.

I'm setting feather count to 11 with thin plate scaling, giving longer back feathers a draping effect, and working out the rotation formula so each radial element aligns along its angle from the fan center.

Now I'm placing the gorget and collar components, attaching the neck chain to a bone around y1.5-1.6, assigning the cuirass to spine2, and adding a dark steel pelvis plate near the hip bone.

Checking tasset clearance against legs and the surcoat front/back panels relative to thigh radius and cape position — making sure panels sit clear of the body at z ±.125-ish. For the griffin decal, I'm positioning it centered on the chest around y1.17 with a size around .2x.28, aligned with the surcoat panel bounds from 1.38 down to .46.

Now I'm sizing the shield's griffin emblem to match the SVG aspect ratio (roughly .77), landing on [.3, .39] centered near y1.08, adjusting slightly since the shield outline narrows toward the bottom and would otherwise clip the griffin's width there.

I'm placing the shield outline at [0.37, 0.98, 0.31], spanning local y from top 1.48 down to tip .43, with its front face sitting just past z=.31. For the rim extrusion I'm keeping the tip corner sharp while smoothing the rest of the outline, and checking that the shield's z-depth clears the left forearm and hand geometry so there's no collision.

I'm adjusting the shield's z-origin to .33 so its back face clears the fingers, placing the decal on its front face, and confirming the left hand sits properly under the shield with the pauldron tucked behind it. Now I'm moving to the right hand sword, positioning the grip, pommel, and guard relative to the wrist bone at x=-.43.

Still writing sword geometry...

Working out joint placement for fingers and thumb, checking that the thumb box sits above the palm with proper vertical contact and doesn't overlap the finger stack.

For the gauntlet I'm thinking steel coloring for the palm and fingers with a darker accent, gold for knuckles. For the cape, I'm computing a point array and using a slab geometry with a stripe pattern for the paint, varying the colors by axis and adding wobble for a weathered look, possibly layering a mottle effect to darken the lower portion.

For grime I'm applying a gradient that darkens toward the bottom edge, blending the stripe paint into a deeper red-black tone, confirming that gradient and slab accept paint-based color fills correctly with surface coordinates.

Now I'm working out the mantle piece over the shoulders using a frustum box shape anchored at the shoulder points, figuring out the direction and perpendicular vectors needed to orient it properly.

I'm deciding to skip the mantle in favor of simpler elements -- a crimson top band on the cape near the spine with clasps, and considering a gold gorget ring for the collar instead of a full trim piece, while skipping rivets on the pauldron for now.

Still placing clasp details...

Now setting up the imports and color constants, then starting the griffin SVG markup for the crest design.

Still writing SVG code...

Adding more filigree circles, then I'm defining the cape's jagged point coordinates and mapping them into 3D space, checking that the resulting polygon doesn't self-intersect for triangulation.

Now I'm setting up a helper for drawing limb bands using position, direction, radius, and bone binding, then looping over left and right sides to build legs, arms, and hands symmetrically. I'm deciding to add the sword only to the right-hand branch and the shield only to the left, and writing a small vector normalization helper for computing forearm direction from wrist and elbow positions.

I'm placing a griffin decal on the front surcoat panel, working out where the frustum-shaped torso panels' faces sit in z so the decal lands flush on the front surface, then moving on to define the cuirass frustum box dimensions and panel edges for the torso.

I'm checking the surcoat and cuirass front plates align in depth, then sketching in a gold trim detail and assigning spine bones for each piece — cuirass to spine2, belt to spine1, hanging panels to spine2, cape to spine3 — before mentally verifying the part-adding function signatures and rotation option format are consistent.

Now I'm working through the remaining geometry helpers: lathe and extrude functions for shapes, a hip joint role setup, and explicit bone parenting for the spine chain. I'm positioning an elbow spike cone pointing backward along the arm, then listing out dent and scratch details, confirming the overall figure height and foot placement, and checking the ankle joint and foot bone alignment.

Now I'm finalizing material colors -- steel for the pelvis, leather described as a string value, a belt piece, and making the boots a darker flat steel tone to match.
